title: Looking the gift horses in the mouth: co-location and outsourcing
author: Ian Anstice / The Library Campaign

editorial.text: An interesting look at the positives and perils of co-location has come from on of the current epicentres of the libraries crisis in Lincolnshire. The Co-Op has offered to take over six libraries and points to the way it has integrated a library into one of its shops. Others, however, point out that the library is tiny and is not the way forward. Faced with cuts and an idea that libraries are no longer necessary (despite the massive protests), however, one suspects which side the Council will choose. Another alternative to council provision of libraries is, of course, the private sector. The boss of JLIS has been talking to the Conservative Way Forward Group about the advantages of doing so: a message one suspects is falling onto fertile ground there. However, all is not as rosy as he suggests with JLIS in Hounslow, as the comments in the article suggest. Also, my article on the pros and cons of outsourcing libraries raises a few questions too – like how the Council gave them £5 million to run it in the first place. See the this page on co-location and this page on outsourcing for more pros and cons.
